question: A baker wants a sharper, more vinegary sourdough. Which change to the starter tilts its acids towards acetic acid?
answer: A stiffer starter kept cool. Warm, wet dough speeds lactic acid most, so heat and water mainly add mild, yogurt-like sourness. Cool, firm dough slows lactic acid more than acetic acid, the sharp acid of vinegar, and the balance shifts towards it. Bakers set a loaf's tang with the starter's water and the thermostat.
move: When one source makes two products, ask which one each condition favours.
trap: Assuming warmth and moisture make every kind of sourness stronger.
source: Gobbetti & Gänzle, Handbook on Sourdough Biotechnology
reference: Gobbetti & Gänzle (eds), Handbook on Sourdough Biotechnology, Springer, 2013
